lifecycle_scope: The macroscopic plasmodium stage is a single large cell containing many nuclei in shared cytoplasm. Species has a multi-stage life cycle; not every stage is a giant cell.

observational_facts.title: Multinucleate plasmodium
observational_facts.description: A large, mobile, single-cell stage containing many nuclei; cytoplasm circulates throughout protoplasmic tubes.

observational_facts.title: Pulsatile cytoplasmic flow
observational_facts.description: Contractile protoplasmic tubes redistribute nutrients and signals, supporting adaptive foraging.

observational_facts.title: Adaptive transport networks
observational_facts.description: Experiments show formation of efficient network configurations that balance transport, length and robustness.

observational_facts.title: Externalized spatial memory
observational_facts.description: Deposited extracellular slime tracks previously explored space and can influence future movement.

observational_facts.title: Non-neural adaptive behavior
observational_facts.description: Some experiments report habituation and other task-dependent adaptive behavior despite lack of neurons and a central brain.

boundaries: Not a fungus. The term slime mold refers to its growth form and life history, not membership in Fungi.
Plasmodium is a multinucleate single-cell stage, not a colony of individual neurons or an artificial general intelligence.
Intelligence is an informal analogy for task-dependent adaptive behavior; no conventional brain, neural synapses, subjective experience or consciousness is established.
Numerical solver is a simplified flow-reinforcement algorithm inspired by Physarum network studies; not a calibrated physiological, growth, or reaction-diffusion prediction.
Generated branch layout, food gradients, printed patterns and SVG are simulated/design outputs; no real organism, living network, implant, neural activity or device is controlled.
No biological culture or hardware is connected; browser interactions never send data to a physical actuator.
